j3.4: The tokenizer splits the text into pieces from a fixed vocabulary and gives each piece an id. First a special token is added that marks the start.
j3.5: Each id looks up a row in the embedding table. Now every token is a vector of 4096 numbers. This is the starting value in the residual stream.
j3.6: Each block lets the positions read from each other (attention) and then processes each position on its own (MLP). The results are added to the stream. After 32 blocks, the last row carries everything needed to guess the next token.
j3.7: x [5, 4096]   same shape, new content. The last row is used.
j3.8: The vector of the last row is multiplied by the LM head. The result is one number per token in the vocabulary: the higher, the more likely the continuation.

j3.10: Softmax turns the logits into probabilities, and one token is drawn. Here it came out as “ mattan”.
j3.11: one id: the token for “ mattan”
j3.13: The new token is appended and everything runs again. But only the new position has to be computed: the keys and values for the first five stay in the KV cache. That is how the response grows, one token per round.

j3.30: MoE: the router picks 2 of 4 experts per layer for “{{tok}}”. Switch token and see that other weight blocks are used. The weights themselves are still the same.
j3.32: Every token has a key and a value, computed from its vector with Wk and Wv. The token being updated, “den”, also has a query: q = {{q}}. The query describes what “den” is looking for.
j3.34: The query is compared with every key. For “Katten”: 1.5·2 + 0.5·0 = 3.0. The highest score goes to the key that points most in the same direction as q.
j3.35: The scores are divided by √2 ≈ 1.41 (in Llama √128 ≈ 11.3). Without that, dot products in many dimensions would get so large that softmax puts all the weight on a single token.
j3.36: exp of each score, divided by the sum. Now the scores are weights that add up to 1: “den” will fetch {{p}}% from “Katten”.
j3.37: The result is the sum: {{out}}. It lies closest to the value of “Katten”, [1, 0]. This vector goes through Wo and is added to the row of “den” in the residual stream. The information about the cat has moved to a new position.

j3.40: “Rows” are positions run through a layer. Without a cache the work grows with the length of the sequence at every step, with a cache it is 2 rows (one per layer).
